title: Supreme Court: IBC Moratorium Shields the Corporate Debtor Alone, Not Its Directors
case_name: Tejas J. Shah v. Mantri Technology Constellations Pvt. Ltd.
card_summary: Homebuyers in a Bengaluru project had their consumer complaint adjourned indefinitely by the NCDRC once the developer entered insolvency, though the complaint also named its promoters and directors. The Supreme Court set the adjournment aside, holding Section 14's moratorium protects only the corporate debtor and cannot freeze proceedings against promoters or directors not themselves under insolvency resolution.
card_tip: A moratorium against one respondent in insolvency is no reason to park an entire consumer or civil complaint; press the forum to proceed against the co-respondents who are not under CIRP.
verification_notes: Case citation (2026 INSC 746), the bench (Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta), the Mantri Manyata Energia project background, the NCDRC's sine die adjournment, and the holding that the Section 14 moratorium is confined to the corporate debtor are consistent across King Stubb & Kasiva's analysis and Legal Suvidha's summary. The judgment text itself was not independently retrieved.
